passage:
Ashtami, 11 pm
Feet are dead. Worth it.
Morning: Dadi woke us at five for the puja. I did the aarti plate this year for the first time! Didn't drop a single diya. Dadi said I held it 'just like your Dada used to'. I don't really know what all the Sanskrit means, but I know every word by heart, same as everyone.
Evening: kanya puja at Sharma Aunty's, then garba till the uncles begged for mercy. Vishal and I won the dandiya round, obviously.
I love how for these nine days the whole lane feels like one family. Nobody asks why we do it. We just do it, together, like every year.
Rajni
PS: tomorrow = halwa-puri 😋

qa.q: What did Rajni do at the morning puja for the first time?
qa.a: Rajni did the aarti plate for the first time.

qa.q: How does Rajni feel about the nine days of festival, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Rajni feels warm and part of something bigger, loving how the whole lane feels like one family and doing it all without asking why.

qa.q: What could Dadi do to keep the ritual meaningful as Rajni grows?
qa.a: Dadi could share what the Sanskrit words mean and the stories behind them, so the warm belonging can grow along with understanding.

qa.q: How might Dadi feel watching Rajni hold the aarti plate?
qa.a: Dadi probably feels proud and moved, seeing Rajni carry a practice that Dada once did 🤍

grounding: It shows a teenager taking part in festival prayers as a warm, unquestioned part of family and neighbourhood life.

passage:
Irawati: you coming for cricket after school?
Asif: can't, fasting 😅 no energy till iftar
Irawati: all day, no water??
Asif: yep. first year I'm doing all 30. Abbu's so proud
Irawati: isn't it hard?
Asif: sometimes. but iftar is the best part. whole family on the floor, dates first, Ammi's pakoras, my cousins fighting over the last samosa
Asif: then I go for night prayers with Abbu and Dadu. half the building is there
Irawati: sounds nice actually
Asif: it's just what we do every year. feels like home x10
Irawati: save me a samosa on Eid
Asif: no promises 😄

qa.q: What does Asif's family eat first at iftar?
How does Asif feel about the fasting month, even when it's hard?
qa.a: Asif feels proud and happy, calling it 'home x10', a warm family time that doesn't need questioning.

qa.q: How could a friend like Irawati respond well to Asif's fasting?
qa.a: Irawati can respect the fast, perhaps move cricket to after iftar, and stay curious without teasing, just as in this chat.

qa.q: What might Irawati learn about Asif's life from this chat?
qa.a: Irawati learns that for Asif the fast is less about hunger and more about family, food and praying together, which is why it 'sounds nice actually'.

grounding: It shows a teenager keeping the fast and night prayers as a normal, warm part of family and community life, without questioning it.
